title: Transient routing incident: customer update + postmortem draft
content:
PURPOSE
This is a draft customer-facing status page update and concise postmortem for the routing/latency incident that affected hosted inference in EU-west on 2026-03-11. Goal: provide a short status message for the public status page and a longer, plain-English postmortem suitable for customers who received degraded responses or model fallbacks.

SHORT STATUS PAGE MESSAGES (two variants)
- Minimal (single line): "Investigating increased latency and occasional model fallbacks in EU-west; mitigation in progress. Updates every 60 minutes."
- Expanded (for incident timeline/updates section): "We observed elevated request queuing and automated routing to smaller model variants for a subset of EU-west traffic, causing intermittent latency and reduced throughput from 08:30–11:45 UTC. We applied capacity shift and routing fixes; normal service restored at 11:45 UTC. Root cause analysis is ongoing."

TEMPLATED CUSTOMER EMAIL / POSTMORTEM (concise, customer-facing)
Subject: Update and postmortem summary — EU-west inference routing incident (2026-03-11)

Hello —

On 2026-03-11 between ~08:30 and 11:45 UTC some customers experienced elevated latency and a small number of requests were routed to lower-capacity model variants by our automated fallback system. We are sorry for the disruption. Below is a brief summary of what happened, who was affected, and what we are doing to prevent recurrence.

Impact summary
- Scope: Hosted API in EU-west region only. No Dedicated or Private deployments affected.
- Symptoms: Increased per-request latency, token streaming delays, and occasional responses produced by smaller compatible model variants (shorter context, slightly different output distribution).
- Customers impacted: ~6% of requests routed through fallback path during peak window. Enterprise tenants with pinned dedicated capacity were unaffected.

Timeline (UTC)
- 08:25: First alerts — latency & queue depth anomalies for EU-west serving pool (auto-detection).
- 08:30: Automated routing policy engaged, some requests directed to fallback model variants to keep requests serving.
- 08:40: On-call SRE began mitigation, increased autoscaling headroom for EU-west; capacity provisioning lag observed.
- 09:05: Temporary configuration tweak deployed to reduce aggressive fallback heuristics.
- 10:10: Observed partial improvement; residual queuing remained for long-sequence workloads.
- 11:15: Additional GPU pool capacity warmed (dedicated standby nodes repopulated into EU-west).
- 11:45: Normal routing restored; monitoring shows latency and error-rate back to baseline.

Root cause (high level, non-sensitive)
An unexpected shift in request mix (higher percentage of long-context generation requests) combined with a delayed capacity scale-up path caused elevated queueing in our EU-west serving pool. To maintain availability, our routing layer applied a conservative fallback policy that directed some traffic to smaller, compatible model variants. Two contributing factors: (1) a tuning parameter in the autoscaler that delayed node warm-up under this specific mix, and (2) a routing threshold that was too sensitive to short-term queue spikes.

What we changed during the incident
- Adjusted routing threshold to reduce unnecessary fallbacks.
- Triggered manual capacity warm-up and rebalanced traffic across GPU pools.
- Disabled a recently-introduced autoscaler behavior for EU-west that increased warm-up latency under long-sequence workloads.

Planned longer-term remediation
- Autoscaler tuning: update warm-up heuristics and add additional warm standby in EU-west for known long-sequence workloads.
- Routing policy improvement: add hysteresis and request-type aware thresholds so fallbacks are less likely for stable traffic spikes.
- Runbook & simulation: create an incident simulation for the specific mix that triggered this event and validate fallback aggressiveness against customer-facing eval prompts.
- Customer notification opt-in: create a small control that allows customers to opt-out of automated model fallbacks (recommend for customers prioritizing deterministic model outputs).

How to tell if you were affected
If you saw higher latency or slightly changed output distributions between 08:30–11:45 UTC from EU-west, your requests were likely part of the impacted cohort. If you have dedicated capacity, you were not affected. We will provide per-tenant logs for enterprise customers who request them.

Recommended short-term customer actions
- If you require absolute output consistency, consider pinning to Dedicated or Private deployment modes or enable our "no-fallback" setting for critical routes (contact your account team).
- For customers using streaming, add a small client-side retry with jitter for streaming connection resets (we recommend exponential backoff starting at 200ms).

Follow-ups and timeline for deliverables
- Detailed technical postmortem (internal): INF-1153, due 2026-03-20.
- Customer-facing postmortem (this doc): publish by 2026-03-14 after legal/ops review.
- Autoscaler and routing policy changes: mitigations validated by 2026-03-21 and deployed to production by 2026-04-01.

Contacts
- Primary contact: Priya Nair (Customer Success) — priya@redwood.ai
- Technical contact: Jordan Kim (SRE lead) — jordan@redwood.ai

APPENDIX: Suggested status page update cadence (for ops)
- 08:35 (initial): "Investigating increased latency in EU-west; some traffic routed to fallback model variants; updates every 30–60 minutes."
- 09:15 (mitigation): "Applying routing adjustments and additional capacity; some customers may still see intermittent delays. ETA: monitoring for stabilization."
- 11:50 (resolved): "Issue mitigated and traffic restored to normal routing. Follow-up postmortem forthcoming."

NOTES / DRAFTING GUIDANCE
- Keep customer-facing language focused on impact and actions — avoid low-level internal telemetry names.
- Be explicit about who was unaffected (Dedicated, Private) to reduce churn.
- Offer per-tenant logs and follow-up technical review for customers who want them.

DRAFT VERSIONS / APPROVALS NEEDED
- Legal review: ensure phrasing around data and fallbacks aligns with contracts.
- Product review: confirm accuracy of planned remediation timeline.
- Ops/SRE: finalize the timeline entries and ETA statements.

END OF DRAFT
